Prune a tractography bundle to non-overlapping, hull-covering tubes

Source: R/prune.R
prune.Rd

prune() is the low-level, tunable engine behind fatten(): it thins a fiber::bundle (or a fiber::bundle_set) down to a subset of streamlines that can be rendered as fat non-overlapping tubes, from a tube radius and overlap_margin that you choose. Reach for prune() directly when you want full control over the tube size and the clearance between tubes (the argument-driven path); reach for fatten() when you would rather rtists pick a visible radius for you, in which case it calls this same selection logic internally. Use it when you build the tubes yourself, from streamlines that carry no per-point or per-streamline radius: you choose a single tube radius, and prune() keeps as many streamlines as possible such that:

  • any two kept tubes (radius plus overlap_margin clearance) stay clear of each other, and

  • the kept tubes still cover the whole convex hull of the original bundle (every point lies within radius of a kept tube).

plot3d() never shrinks tubes or drops streamlines on its own; it renders whatever radius the object carries. So prune() is the tool to reach for when you fabricate fat tubes from line-only data and want to make sure the overlap was not introduced by you.

The selection is greedy and deterministic, preferring streamlines that sit farthest from the already-kept tubes so the retained set spreads across the bundle rather than clustering.

Usage

prune(x, radius, overlap_margin = 1, ...)

Arguments

x

A fiber::bundle or fiber::bundle_set to prune.

radius

Positive number. The tube radius (world units) used both for the non-overlap clearance and for the hull-coverage test.

overlap_margin

Numeric. Multiplier on the centre-to-centre clearance between kept tubes. The default 1 keeps tubes exactly at radius so they just touch; a value above 1 leaves a visible gap (and a value below 1 would let them interpenetrate, which is allowed but rarely wanted).

...

Reserved for future arguments.

Value

An object of the same class as x holding the pruned subset of streamlines. For a fiber::bundle_set the pruning is applied to every bundle independently, and empty bundles are dropped from the returned set.

See also

fatten(), plot3d(). fatten() is the convenience wrapper that derives the radius for you and calls this engine internally.
